seasonMovement: Impossible arrival -> settlement -> navigation -> participation -> belonging -> usefulness -> choice -> recognition -> self-defined belonging under judgment.
seasonDramaticShift: Issues 1–5 are driven largely by collision with 2026 and the work of building an ordinary life. From Issue 6 forward, modern systems remain real pressure but stop being the default dramatic protagonist. The later season is driven by what these particular people want from work, one another, New York, privacy, autonomy, and belonging.

issues.title: Landfall Bushwick
issues.function: Apartment adaptation and neighborhood integration; the temporary shelter becomes a functioning household while Carrie secures a provisional administrative foothold.

issues.title: The Iron Worm
issues.function: Transit adaptation; Gunnar learns the city as navigable terrain and uses that knowledge to complete the errand and lead the group home

issues.title: The Tally of Dishonor
issues.function: Financial legibility, value, status, and partial civic participation

issues.title: The Skaldic Interface
issues.function: Neighborhood-memory and emerging belonging; recurring relationships and ordinary routines show the Vikings beginning to live independently in New York
issues.status: production-ready 24-page enhanced script encoded in RexPrompt

issues.title: Trial of Toil
issues.function: Bjorn's crisis over usefulness becomes a character story about respect, consent, responsibility, and meaningful contribution. The temporal-refugee group changes how he leads, while the apartment and neighborhood prove whether that change survives ordinary life.
issues.status: enhanced 24-page dramatic spine locked; panel/dialogue script pass pending

issues.title: War Council
issues.function: A Status Reconciliation Review forces the household to decide what it actually wants to defend. The core conflict is not the paperwork but the discovery that staying in New York, staying together, choosing permanence, and preserving individual freedom are not the same decision.
issues.status: enhanced 24-page dramatic spine locked; panel/dialogue pass pending

issues.title: The Filing of Grievances
issues.function: The household revisits the relationships accumulated all season and discovers that being known by other people is different from controlling how those people describe you. Privacy, mixed testimony, first-person voice, and imperfect recognition shape the response before the hearing.
issues.beatCoverage: 47-52 reinterpreted through relationship and voice rather than audit procedure
issues.status: enhanced 24-page dramatic spine locked; panel/dialogue pass pending

issues.title: Permanent Residency / Trial by Combat
issues.function: The residency hearing tests whether an institution can make a fair decision about a real but unconventional household whose members have chosen belonging without surrendering separate identities or future choices.
issues.status: normalized; exact ruling and full enhanced page structure unresolved

finaleState.ordeal: The residency hearing functions as Bjorn's trial by combat without literal combat.
finaleState.hearingPurpose: The hearing is not the climax of a paperwork story. It is where the institution encounters a household that cannot honestly be reduced to one spokesperson, one integration narrative, or one permanent future.
finaleState.bjorn: Bjorn arrives in armor. His growth is visible in using authority to defend other people's right to speak and choose, not in abandoning forceful leadership.
finaleState.carrie: Carrie does not ask him to remove it. She argues the process without pretending the file is the whole truth of the people in it.
